threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still flinch when you see an 'Expected Wait Time' sign at the bus stop, thinking it’s a cruel joke.
Caught a 59 last week, a bloke was trying to sell his mix tape to the driver. The driver just shook his head, but the mixtape was fire!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the kebab shop started recognizing my order and the owner asks about my weekend plans. That's when I felt truly at home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: There's a hidden taco truck in Görlitzer Park that only shows up after 10 PM. It's like a secret club where the late-night crowds gather for late-night bites.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they subtly dodge the dog on the tracks at Civic Center while still sipping their Blue Bottle.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus the other day where the driver paused to rescue a pigeon caught in the door. Only in SF would public transit become a rescue mission.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume all the best tapas spots are on the main square, but the hidden gems are just down the side streets where the locals gather.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their meticulous effort to order in perfect Catalan at local cafes, while locals already know it's just 'un cafè, si us plau.'

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'Hackney' like it’s the whole borough instead of 'Dalston' or 'Stokey'. You’re gonna get called out soon.
Caught two blokes arguing over a missing shoe on the 59 last night. One was convinced it’d magically return at Stockwell. Classic Brixton madness.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Heard a toddler arguing with their parent over what flavor of ice cream they should get outside Eiscafé Bacio. That’s when it hit me—this place feels like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand with its own mini disco ball. It’s the last place you'd expect to dance while waiting for your snack!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by their eye roll when someone suggests renting bikes to explore; we prefer our worn-out shoes and the bus, thank you.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo waiting for the bus, umbrella in hand, while the rain poured down. Only in SF do we dress for the occasion, no matter the transport.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but it’s the small plazas and hidden bars that keep us coming back, not the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confusion over the 15-minute rule at local cafés—waiting for someone to bring the bill instead of asking for it.
